## **ORDER** 

The Petitioner, R.K.M. Powergen Private Limited (in short ‘RKMPPL’), has filed 

the present Petition seeking the following relief(s): 

_“a) Hold and declare that the notification dated 07.12.2015 issued by the Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), requiring installation of Flue Gas Desulphurizer (FGD) and associated systems, constitutes as a change in law event, within the meaning of Article 10 of the PPA dated 15.03.2016, executed between the Petitioner and the Respondent No.1;_ 

_b) Allow in-principal approval for the proposed expenditure to be incurred towards the Change in Law event in relation to procurement, installation, commissioning, operation & maintenance of Flue Gas Desulphurizer (FGD) and associated systems, along with carrying costs as per the provisions of PPA, subject to true up;_ 

_(c) Device a methodology for the purpose of recovery of the amount incurred/ to be incurred by the Petitioner, in installing the FGD and associated systems, along with the methodology towards calculating tariff in relation to the estimated increase in O&M Expenses, other operating norms like Auxiliary Power Consumption and SHR, spares, water charges, landed cost of reagents, gypsum disposal cost etc., with corresponding increase in Capacity Charges and energy charge rate (ECR), as a result of complying with the change in law event of installation of FGD and associated systems such that the Petitioner is restored to the same economic position as if such Change in Law event had not occurred;_ 

_(d) While considering prayers (b) and (c) above, issue directions for exclusion of the period of shutdown (required for installation of FGD) for the purposes of calculating the Availability of the power project of the Petitioner, in order to ensure full recovery of Capacity Charges due to such shutdown;_ 

_(e) Grant liberty to the Petitioner to approach this Hon’ble Commission, after installation of the FGD equipment, for the purpose of true up/ reimbursement of the actual amount,_

_and to claim any other amount not included in the present petition, along with applicable carrying cost/ interest cost, if any;_ 

_(f) Approve and grant carrying costs/ interest costs to the Petitioner from the effective date of the change in law events as claimed in the present petition;_ 

_(g) Direct UPPCL, in future, to continue to make any payments, which will be accruing in favour of the Petitioner, on account of the change in law events, as prayed in the present Petition;_ 

_(h) pass any other order as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice.”_ 

2. The Petitioner, a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956, has set up a 4x360 MW coal-based thermal generating station at Ucchpinda Village, JanjgirChampa District, Chhattisgarh. Pursuant to the competitive bidding process conducted by the Respondent, UPPCL, the bid submitted by the Petitioner for the supply of 350 MW power was accepted, and thereafter, a PPA dated 15.3.2016 was executed between the parties, for a term of 25 years. 

3. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) issued a notification on 7 December 2015 requiring thermal power plants to install additional emission control systems, including Flue Gas Desulphurization (FGD) units, to meet the revised environmental standards. To comply with the said direction, the Petitioner conducted a feasibility study and selected wet limestone-based FGD technology. The Petitioner issued a Change in Law notice to UPPCL on 1st September 2018, relying on the directions of the Ministry of Power and relevant regulatory orders supporting recovery of FGD-related costs. Pursuant to the notification of the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021, the Petitioner issued a fresh notice on 30 December 2021 and the same was rejected by the Respondent, UPPCL, on 20 January 2022. In terms of the APTEL judgment in related matters, the Petitioner

again issued a Change in Law notice on 28 November 2023, but UPPCL rejected the same as well on 21 December 2023 . 

4. In this background, the Petitioner filed the instant Petition. During the first hearing on 7.10.2024, notice was issued, subject to just exceptions and parties were directed to complete the pleadings. Respondent UPPCL, in its reply dated 6 November 2024, challenged the Petition on various grounds, including limitation, maintainability, and non-compliance with the Change in Law provisions of the PPA. 

## **Hearing dated 25.5.2026** 

5. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that in terms of the MoEFCC notification dated 11.7.2025, the generating station of the Petitioner stands classified under Category ‘C’, pursuant to which the requirement of the FGD systems is no longer required. Therefore, upon instructions, the learned counsel for the Petitioner requested to withdraw the present Petition. The learned counsel appearing for the Respondents did not object to the said request. 

6. In view of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner and in the absence of any objection from the Respondents, the prayer for withdrawal of the instant Petition is allowed. 

7. Accordingly, Petition No. 191/MP/2024 is disposed of as ‘withdrawn’.
